title: The `or default` Idiom
summary: `value or fallback` returns value when it's truthy, otherwise the fallback — the classic one-line default. Remember: only nil and false fall through, so legitimate false values get replaced.

details.heading: Evaluation rule
details.body: `a or b` evaluates `a`; if it's truthy, the expression is `a` — otherwise it's `b`. `b` is only evaluated when needed (short-circuit).

explanation.whatItIs: A compact 'use this, else that' expression built on truthiness.
explanation.whyItExists: Defaulting optional arguments and missing table fields is constant; one operator covers it.
whenToUse: Safe chain fallbacks: `local name = player and player.Name or "unknown"`
whenNotToUse: When false/0/"" are meaningful values — false falls through! Compare against nil explicitly instead
tips: Pairs with `and`: `(cond and a or b)` is Luau's ternary — but beware `a` being falsy
For true ternary behavior on falsy values, use `if ... then ... else ...` expressions
commonMistakes: `enabled or true` can never produce false
Forgetting the right side still RUNS when the left is falsy — avoid expensive calls

examples.title: Defaults in practice
examples.code:
local function spawnEnemy(options)
    options = options or {}
    local hp = options.hp or 100
    local speed = options.speed or 16
    local boss = options.boss      -- may be false on purpose!
    -- ❌ options.boss or false  would hide a deliberate false
    print(hp, speed, boss)
end

spawnEnemy()                    --> 100 16 nil
spawnEnemy({ hp = 50 })         --> 50 16 nil
spawnEnemy({ boss = false })    --> 100 16 false
